## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (six single-source suggestions, one suggestion-level checklist FAIL, thirty-four inconclusive checklist items)
The PR is ready to merge: no reviewer or checklist item found a defect at or above the Important threshold, and every one of the sixteen acceptance criteria has its own checklist item.
Rule applied: rule 6 — only findings below the threshold and inconclusive checklist items remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (7)

<details><summary>7 items</summary>

1. The rule for which database URL schemes are supported is written four times, and the checks differ. `src/sqllens/config.py` lines 109-116 (`DatabaseConfig._supported_url_scheme`) accepts only `mysql`, `mysql+…` and `sqlite…`. `build_sql_runner` (`src/sqllens/agent/factory.py`), `probe_database` (`src/sqllens/preflight.py`) and `sqlglot_dialect_for_url` (`src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py`) each test only `startswith("mysql")`. A `mysqlx://` URL that skips config validation therefore still builds a MySQL runner. Config loading itself behaves correctly. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. The comment on `_SQLGLOT_DIALECT_MAP` in `src/sqllens/eval/compare.py` lines 13-17 says the map translates URL schemes. Its two remaining keys, `mssql` and `mariadb`, can no longer reach it, because config loading now refuses both schemes. The `mariadb` entry also suggests MariaDB support, which the project rules out. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. In `tests/unit/test_safety.py` lines 1195-1205, the new `("mysql", "sleep(0)", "Nested MySQL comments")` row of `test_call_after_nested_comment_markers_is_checked` does not test what the test name says. Under MySQL, the nested-comment refusal rejects the statement before the function denylist sees `sleep(0)`. The `sqlite` row still covers the denylist path, and lines 1145 and 1178 already cover the nested-comment refusal. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. In `src/sqllens/safety/relations.py` lines 112-114, under a dialect with no table entry, `verify_base_tables` returns without logging or refusing for a query that references no table but calls a function. Acceptance criterion 9 requires this behavior. The shipped runners pass only `mysql` or `sqlite`, so only a custom runner wrapped by `RlsGuardRunner` can reach this path. The docstring does not mention the pass-through. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `docs/external/configuration.md` lines 44-47, `README.md` line 61 and `changelog.d/387.removed.md` line 5 say any `mysql+<driver>://` URL loads. They do not say that SQL Lens ignores the driver name and always connects with PyMySQL. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. In `docs/internal/index.md` line 34, the subject is now singular ("the MySQL `SqlRunner` implementation swallows…"), but the row still continues "what they log when they do". (raised by 1/6 agents)
- VC-25: FAIL (suggestion) — Each runner (MySQL and SQLite) calls cursor.fetchmany(self._max_rows + 1) and builds the result through rows_to_capped_df; the MySQL runner uses SSDictCursor and does not call cursor.close() on the SELECT path. [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:117]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Only two runners exist under src/sqllens/agent/integrations (mysql/sql_runner.py, sqlite/sql_runner.py; complete Glob listing), so no runner uses fetchall or another batch pattern. Verified parts: both read paths call cursor.fetchmany(cap + 1) then rows_to_capped_df(rows, cap) (mysql sql_runner.py:151-153; sqlite sql_runner.py:216-218). MySQL SELECT path uses conn.cursor(self.pymysql.cursors.SSDictCursor) (line 149) and never calls cursor.close() on it (returns at 153; the only cursor.close() at 166 is the non-read DictCursor write path; teardown is conn.close() at 182). Not matching: the authored doc (docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:117) says the call is `cursor.fetchmany(self._max_rows + 1)`, but neither runner passes self._max_rows+1: both compute cap = effective_row_cap(self._max_rows) (limits.py:36-54 returns min(constructor_cap, effective.max_rows) when per-request effective settings are bound) and call fetchmany(cap + 1). With a per-request profile that narrows max_rows, the batch size is narrower than self._max_rows + 1, so the literal claim is wrong. This wording is unchanged from base (base line 122, same text); the PR only removed the Postgres sentence. The +1 sentinel semantics and the SSDictCursor/no-close behaviour are correct, so the defect is a minor doc imprecision.

  </details>

</details>

- VC-30: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — MySQL's `TABLE t` shorthand is refused on every supported sqlglot version (>=30.22,<31), found by uses_table_shorthand before the root-type check. [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:33]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Ordering half is confirmed. In src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py, assert_select_only parses first (_parse_statements, line 592), then calls uses_table_shorthand(sql, dialect) at lines 593-596 and raises UnsafeSqlError, and only afterwards runs the statement-count check (598) and the root-type check (607/620). So the shorthand scan runs before the root-type check, as the claim says. Trace of the falsifying inputs through uses_table_shorthand (lines 79-121): comments are not tokens, so '/* c */ TABLE t' gives previous='' and returns True. A quoted or backticked `TABLE` is an IDENTIFIER token, not TokenType.TABLE, so it is not flagged, and it is not a shorthand either. A quoted identifier or string before TABLE resets previous to '' (119-120), so it cannot exempt one. The exempting predecessors ('.', CREATE, SHOW, EXPLAIN, ANALYZE and so on) cannot precede a real TABLE-t query operand; valid positions such as start, ';', '(', ')', UNION/ALL/DISTINCT and AS ( all return True. _mysql_parse_sql (477-534) only rewrites CR inside comments, so tokenizing the original SQL should match tokenizing the sanitized SQL on the supported >=30.22 tokenizers. A TokenError would return False only where _parse_statements has already raised. Tests at tests/unit/test_safety_table_shorthand.py and tests/unit/test_safety.py:720-728 cover these cases for mysql, sqlite and None. What I cannot settle is the library fact the claim rests on: that on every sqlglot version in >=30.22,<31 the MySQL tokenizer emits TokenType.TABLE for an unquoted `table` and does not fold it into a multi-word keyword. The item has no dependency_sources and the view inventory has no sqlglot source (searched inventory.json for sqlglot/tokens.py and sqlglot/dialects/mysql.py: none). I did not run the tests across the version range, and the claim covers every version in it, so I did not read the .venv copy of sqlglot as a substitute. Missing evidence: sqlglot tokens.py KEYWORDS and the MySQL tokenizer for 30.22 through the latest 30.x, or a test run across those versions. No counterexample was found in the repository code.

  </details>

In src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py, assert_select_only parses first (_parse_statements, line 592), then calls uses_table_shorthand(sql, dialect) at lines 593-596 and raises UnsafeSqlError, and only afterwards runs the statement-count check (598) and the root-type check (607/620). So the shorthand scan runs before the root-type check, as the claim says. Trace of the falsifying inputs through uses_table_shorthand (lines 79-121): comments are not tokens, so '/* c */ TABLE t' gives previous='' and returns True. A quoted or backticked `TABLE` is an IDENTIFIER token, not TokenType.TABLE, so it is not flagged, and it is not a shorthand either. A quoted identifier or string before TABLE resets previous to '' (119-120), so it cannot exempt one.
